findings.desc: packages/main/src/cli-engine.ts:767-784 — HIGH: runtime-authority gate is installed only at lines 860-882, after early-return branches. A stale global runtime invoked from a linked self-host worktree can run `init` (which imports self-executing cli-init.js and writes project files) or start `dashboard` without ever calling classifyRuntimeEntrypointAuthority. This violates the claimed pre-dispatch zero-mutation boundary and the policy that only explicit global-fallback session_brief is exempt. Move/classify the authority boundary before all executable early returns (while preserving help/version as an explicit, mechanically narrow policy if desired) and add hermetic stale-global init/dashboard negative controls proving zero writes/process start.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 2401277417. The raw-argv authority preflight now runs immediately after root and alias normalization and before init/dashboard/tool/phase/schema/Store/hooks/handler/validation. findings.desc: packages/main/src/cli-engine.ts:767-785,795-847 — HIGH: runtime authority is enforced only at line 868, after standalone init/dashboard execution and after tool/phase/schema exits. Therefore a self-host worktree invoked through the stale main runtime can run init (and start the long-lived dashboard) without any authority classification, while a worktree-only command or newer argument is rejected by the stale registry/schema before the canonical local-entrypoint recovery can be emitted. This contradicts CHK-001 edge:2 (all commands except explicit fallback session_brief remain subject to classification) and CHK-002/adversarial:0 (reject before mutating/expensive work). Move a raw-argv-safe authority preflight immediately after root/alias normalization and before standalone commands/tool lookup; retain only help/version as an explicitly reasoned exemption, then add E2E assertions for stale init/dashboard and a command unknown to main but valid locally.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 2401277417. Guard placement now precedes standalone commands, tool lookup and schema validation.
